### Paris Family Adventure Overview

Here is a 5-day itinerary for your family trip to Paris, designed for a relaxed pace with a mix of iconic landmarks and child-focused activities. The plan keeps your budget of $3000 USD in mind, focusing on pre-booked tickets to save time and ensuring no activities extend past 9 PM. For local transport, a Navigo Découverte weekly pass for each family member is the most cost-effective option for your Monday-to-Friday trip.

### 5-Day Paris Itinerary

**Day 1: Montmartre Charm (Monday, Aug 12)**
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e4/Montmartre_in_Paris_France_2.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/palette.svg
- Arrive and settle into your accommodation.
- In the late afternoon, take the funicular up to the charming hilltop neighborhood of Montmartre.
- Admire the Sacré-Cœur Basilica from the outside and enjoy the panoramic city views from its steps.
- For a fun and easy dinner, find a local crêperie for a variety of sweet and savory crêpes that are sure to please everyone.

**Day 2: Iconic Sights & Seine Views (Tuesday, Aug 13)**
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a3/Bateaux_Mouche_sur_la_Seine_%282559051392%29.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- Start your day with a pre-booked morning visit to the Eiffel Tower. Going to the top offers an unforgettable experience for the whole family.
- After lunch, embark on a relaxing Seine River Cruise. It’s a fantastic way to see many of Paris's famous landmarks from a different perspective without tiring out little legs.
- Choose a classic bistro for dinner; many offer simple, kid-friendly dishes like *steak frites* (steak and fries).

**Day 3: Royal Art & Garden Play (Wednesday, Aug 14)**
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/1d/Jardin_des_Tuileries_28_02_2007_N1.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Visit the Louvre Museum in the morning. To keep children engaged, plan a "treasure hunt" to find famous masterpieces like the Mona Lisa, the Venus de Milo, and the Winged Victory of Samothrace.
- In the afternoon, head next door to the Jardin des Tuileries. Enjoy a picnic lunch and let the kids burn off energy by the grand basin, where they can rent and sail model boats.

**Day 4: A Day of Science & Discovery (Thursday, Aug 15)**
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/54/Cit%C3%A9_des_sciences_et_de_l%27industrie_-_La_Villette_-_Paris_2010.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/lightbulb.svg
- Dedicate the day to the Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie, one of Europe's largest science museums.
- The interactive exhibits and the dedicated "Cité des Enfants" (Children's City) for different age groups provide a full day of hands-on learning and fun.
- For dinner, consider a casual pizzeria or a traditional "bouillon" restaurant, known for serving classic French dishes at affordable prices.

**Day 5: Parisian Gardens & Farewell (Friday, Aug 16)**
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/87/Jardin_du_Luxembourg_in_Paris_September_2013.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/joystick.svg
- Spend your final morning at the beautiful Jardin du Luxembourg. The park features a fantastic playground, pony rides, and a traditional puppet theater (*Théâtre des Marionnettes*).
- Enjoy a final Parisian lunch in the nearby Latin Quarter and do some last-minute souvenir shopping.
- Head to the airport for your departure, filled with family memories.

### Dining Tips for Young Travelers

Paris offers many simple and delicious options perfect for children, even picky eaters. Look for these items on menus:
- **Crêpes:** Available with savory fillings (*galettes*) like ham and cheese or sweet fillings like Nutella or sugar.
- **Croque Monsieur:** A classic grilled ham and cheese sandwich, often served with a side of fries or salad.
- **Steak Frites:** A simple dish of a pan-fried steak served with french fries. A staple in most bistros.
- **Poulet Rôti:** Roast chicken is widely available and a familiar comfort food for many children.
- **Jambon-Beurre:** The quintessential Parisian sandwich: a fresh baguette with butter and ham.
- **From the Boulangerie:** For breakfast or snacks, you can't go wrong with croissants, *pain au chocolat*, and fresh baguettes.
